$comment: The one definition of every agent, owned by Controller: one row per package under packages/. Every other declaration of an agent is generated from this file or checked against it by npm run check:agents-definition. `lists` are the named, ordered agent lists code reads instead of writing one out; `handoffs` are the chain edges; `ladder` is the readiness ladder, whose rungs are computed into docs/contracts/agents.rungs.json. Packages read them through the generated copies `node scripts/check-agents-definition.mjs --write` writes.

ladder.description: The one readiness ladder, owned by Controller. An agent's rung is computed, never declared: `clossys agents check` runs each rung's check in order and writes the highest rung whose check, and every check below it, passes to docs/contracts/agents.rungs.json (generated). Each check runs in root `check` for every agent the generated file places at or above its rung.

rungs.means: The agent's row and every other declaration of it (role contract, evidence, lifecycle, wave, release qualification, renames, package.json, skill name, lists, generated copies) agree.
The conformance gate, run with --enforce, reports no gap and no finding for the agent's package.
A retained release-qualification record exists for the package's current version, under its published name.
The package ships its skill and every command (bin) it declares, and check:bin-reachability and check:install-docs pass for it.
The agent's check:agents entries pass, and clossys init adopts its loops (it is in the content list and ships loops/).

needs.description: Every agent in the install list (clossys init, the pack script and Advisor's front door read it) needs rung packed or higher; `clossys agents check` exits 1 while one is below it and reports the computed set next to the list.

content.description: The content agents in chain order. Each owns slots, a loop and a queue. Its members are exactly the rows of class content.

live.description: The agents with a live record tree under clossys/agents: the content agents in chain order, then Producer.

nav.description: The live agents in Studio nav and interview order: Producer, then the content agents in chain order.

e2e.description: The first-party packages the end-to-end check installs and the overlay cohort packs: the nav agents, then Controller.

install.description: The roles a consumer install pack holds, each exactly once: what pack-five packs and advisor install accepts.

placed.description: The agents whose package IA places slots in a consumer; Publisher assembles and places none.

policy.description: The agents whose owner decisions are asked as policy, not per slot.

copy-keys.description: The agents whose slot candidates carry copy keys and declared inputs.

markdown.description: The agents whose candidates are Markdown documents; the others' are JSON.

surfaces.description: The packages that ship rendered surfaces: Designer's components and Publisher's pages.

side-door.description: The packages the engine side-door scan reads, in scan order.

assemble-only.description: The agent words the assemble-only check reads in a page or route, in match order.

native-cells.description: The roles whose package framework declares native cells.

trio.description: The first three packages ever published: the pre-cutover release target and the first wave of qualification.

release-order.description: Every published package in release order; Producer is not published.

release-receivers.description: The agents a Publisher release hands over to, one per destination kind: what a release target, handover and receipt may name.

coverage-externals.description: The packages whose catalogs Designer's IA coverage reads as external nodes: Writer's passages and copy records, Publisher's admin routes and compositions.

provenance-stamped.description: The packages whose sources, tests and scripts the DOM provenance attribute codemods rewrite and check.

handoffs.description: The chain handoffs (flows.md N3): Director feeds Designer and Writer, and Designer and Writer feed Publisher. Each pair is upstream, then downstream.
